Today's rules, in order: the gate (422), the inputs, one active search per user (409 with

get.description:
The rows a run card lists (`output.topMatchIds` or `output.matchIds`). Anything that is
not a UUID is ignored; at most 20; another user's ids find nothing.

post.description:
Queues a deep evaluation and answers at once: it takes tens of seconds, which is not a
request's to wait for. Throttled (`evaluate:<user>`, 60 an hour).
Stores the file (if it is new) and starts reading it; the run does the reading (§11.1).

get.description:
An uploaded resume or a rendered PDF, for its owner only. Inline by default, so a PDF opens
in the browser's viewer; `?download=1` makes it an attachment. Never cached.

put.description:
Validated, then diffed against the newest base version so only the items the user really
changed become `source: "user"` (§11.3); a save that changes nothing writes nothing.

gets one.

SettingsOut.description: The user's settings with the defaults applied: every field is always present.
SettingsOut.title: SettingsOut

SettingsPatch.description: Any subset of the settings. Unknown keys and nulls are refused.
SettingsPatch.title: SettingsPatch

MatchPatch.description:
Any of the four; a field left out is left alone, `null` clears notes or the rating.

`stageChangedAt` goes only with `stage`: the board's Undo sends the time the match had
entered the stage it goes back to, so an undone move leaves "found … ago" as it was (a
later time than now is taken as now).

`laneOverride` puts the match in the apply lane the user chose (`matching/lanes.py`), and
`null` hands it back to the review.
MatchPatch.title: MatchPatch

CompanyRow.description: One company as the companies page shows it (`company-row.ts`'s `CompanyRow`).
CompanyRow.title: CompanyRow

AnswerKind.description:
The questions application forms share. `custom` is any other question, kept under the
question's own words.
AnswerKind.title: AnswerKind

FillPayload.description: One application as the extension fills it (`extension.payload`).
FillPayload.title: FillPayload

OnboardingState.description:
Where one user stands between signing up and a first search: one answer, read the same way
by Home, Profile, Matches and the agent (`map/_gaps.md` §3.7, minus `hasProfile`).
OnboardingState.title: OnboardingState

seniority_fit.description: The candidate against the posting's level: under = the role asks for more experience than they have; over = they are overqualified.
seniority_fit.title: Seniority Fit

salary_fit.description: The posting's pay against the candidate's salary floor: above = pays more than their floor; below = pays less.
salary_fit.title: Salary Fit

JobFacts.description:
What the posting asks of whoever applies (`jobs/facts.py`, #56), with the sentence each
was read from. `read` is false until the posting's facts have been read.
JobFacts.title: JobFacts

MatchApplication.description: The match's application, when one has been prepared or is being (#60).
MatchApplication.title: MatchApplication

Radar.description: How soon new postings are seen and how often boards are asked (`jobs/radar.py`, #55).
Radar.title: Radar

ApplyAnswer.description: One field of an application's form with the answer planned for it (`prepare.Planned`).
ApplyAnswer.title: ApplyAnswer

ApplyResume.description: Which resume an application sends, and why (`applications/resume.py`, #61).
ApplyResume.title: ApplyResume

OutcomesPage.description:
How long applications took to go out and what came of them (`applications/outcomes.py`,
#65, #6). Every number comes with the count it rests on; a rate is null on too few.
OutcomesPage.title: OutcomesPage

SavedAnswer.description: One of the questions application forms share (#21), with the user's answer if any.
SavedAnswer.title: SavedAnswer

ExtensionTokenRow.description:
One of the user's browser-extension tokens (#22). The secret itself was shown once,
when it was made; only its hash is kept, so there is nothing more to show.
ExtensionTokenRow.title: ExtensionTokenRow

sections.description: Limit to these sections. Null reads the whole resume, which is usually what you want.
sections.title: Sections

name_or_url.description: A company name ("Stripe"), a domain, or a job-board URL.
name_or_url.title: Name Or Url

count.description: How many companies to look for. Keep it modest.
count.title: Count

prompt.description: What the user asked for, in their own words.
prompt.title: Prompt

companies.description: Companies to limit the search to, when the user names any ("at Anthropic"). Unknown companies are looked up and added automatically.
companies.title: Companies

roles.description: Kinds of role for this search, as short titles ("software engineer").
roles.title: Roles

seniority.description: Level for this search when the user states one. "Entry-level", "junior" or "most entry-level" is entry.
seniority.title: Seniority

locations.description: Places for this search, when the user names any.
locations.title: Locations

remote.description: Remote preference for this search, only when the user states one.
remote.title: Remote

focus.description: Anything else about this search that should shape the ranking, in one sentence ("lowest experience requirements first").
focus.title: Focus

mode.description: approve_each pauses before deep evaluation and before shortlisting; autopilot does both without asking. Null uses the user's default from settings — only set it when they say which they want.
mode.title: Mode

run_id.description: Only the roles this search run found, or this watch run announced.
run_id.title: Run Id

query.description: Text to match in title or company.
query.title: Query

note.description: A short note to add to the role's notes (e.g. who they spoke to), or null.
note.title: Note
